title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Opinions on Several Issues concerning Giving Full Play to the Role of Intellectual Property Adjudication in Promoting the Great Development and Prosperity of Socialist Culture and Promoting Independent and Coordinated Economic Development
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Issuance of the "Opinions on Fully Leveraging the Functional Role of Intellectual Property Adjudication to Promote the Great Development and Prosperity of Socialist Culture and Facilitate the Autonomous and Coordinated Development of the Economy"

Fa Fa [2011] No. 18

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Supreme People's Court's "Opinions on Fully Leveraging the Functional Role of Intellectual Property Adjudication to Promote the Great Development and Prosperity of Socialist Culture and Facilitate the Autonomous and Coordinated Development of the Economy" are hereby issued to you for careful implementation in accordance with the actual work of adjudication. Please report any issues encountered during implementation to this Court without delay.

December 16, 2011

Opinions on Fully Leveraging the Functional Role of Intellectual Property Adjudication to Promote the Great Development and Prosperity of Socialist Culture and Facilitate the Autonomous and Coordinated Development of the Economy

To thoroughly implement the spirit of the Sixth Plenary Session of the 17th Central Committee and the Central Economic Work Conference, and the requirements outlined in the Outline of the Twelfth Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development, and to fully leverage the functional role of intellectual property adjudication in promoting the great development and prosperity of socialist culture, accelerating the transformation of the economic development model, and facilitating the autonomous and coordinated development of the economy, the following opinions are hereby put forward on relevant issues:

I. Emancipate the Mind, Engage in Active Justice, and Effectively Strengthen the Sense of Responsibility and Mission in Providing Judicial Protection for Intellectual Property

1. Raise awareness and effectively enhance the initiative and proactivity in promoting the great development and prosperity of socialist culture and facilitating the autonomous and coordinated development of the economy. The "Decision of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Major Issues Concerning Deepening Cultural System Reform and Promoting the Great Development and Prosperity of Socialist Culture," adopted at the Sixth Plenary Session of the 17th Central Committee, defines the path of socialist cultural development with Chinese characteristics, establishes the strategic goal of building a socialist cultural powerhouse, and sets forth the guiding ideology, objectives, tasks, important policies, and major measures for promoting cultural reform and development under the new circumstances. It is a programmatic document guiding China's socialist cultural construction for the current and future periods. The Outline of the Twelfth Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development clearly states that all work in the next five years must take scientific development as the theme and accelerating the transformation of the economic development model as the main thread; adhere to making strategic economic restructuring the main direction of attack and regard technological progress and innovation as important supports. The Central Economic Work Conference requires firmly grasping the solid foundation of developing the real economy and striving to create a social atmosphere that encourages down-to-earth work, hard work to start businesses, and getting rich through industry; firmly grasping the powerful driving force of accelerating reform and innovation, seizing the opportunity to achieve breakthroughs in key areas and crucial links as soon as possible, focusing on improving original innovation capabilities, and continuously enhancing integrated innovation, and the ability to introduce, digest, absorb, and re-innovate; adhering to innovation-driven development and strengthening intellectual property protection; cultivating and developing strategic emerging industries, focusing on promoting major technological breakthroughs and enhancing core competitiveness; accelerating the expansion of the cultural industry and promoting the vigorous development of cultural undertakings. Cultural development, technological progress, and knowledge innovation are the fundamental driving forces for transforming the economic development model and achieving autonomous and coordinated economic development. Intellectual property protection is closely related to promoting cultural development, prosperity, and autonomous and coordinated economic development. Courts at all levels and the vast majority of intellectual property judges must fully recognize the situation, effectively enhance their awareness of the overall situation and sense of responsibility, adhere to active justice, identify the right combination points and entry points, and in the judicial protection of intellectual property, pay more attention to incentivizing cultural development and technological progress, pay more attention to promoting cultural innovation and developing new cultural business forms, pay more attention to promoting the development and prosperity of intellectual property culture; pay more attention to leveraging the role of intellectual property in promoting and guiding the real economy, pay more attention to cultivating and developing strategic emerging industries and promoting strategic economic restructuring, pay more attention to improving China's comprehensive national strength and international competitiveness, and fully play the role of builders and guarantors in promoting the great development and prosperity of socialist culture and the autonomous and coordinated development of the economy.

2. Update concepts and effectively enhance the targetedness and effectiveness of serving the great development and prosperity of socialist culture and the autonomous and coordinated development of the economy. Strengthen the concept of enhanced protection, fully recognizing that enhanced protection is the main contradiction, basic positioning, and policy orientation of current intellectual property judicial protection, coordinate both domestic and international situations, make full and good use of intellectual property laws, strengthen judicial protection for all types of intellectual property, effectively reduce the cost of rights protection, and increase the intensity of sanctions. Strengthen the concept of categorization and appropriate leniency and strictness, paying attention to adapting to the attributes and characteristics of various types of intellectual property in judicial protection, meeting the functions and protection needs of different types of intellectual property, so that intellectual property judicial protection is more adapted to the international and domestic development environment in which China is situated, more in line with the new stage characteristics of China's economic, social, and cultural development, and more in line with the new requirements of China's cultural development and technological innovation. Strengthen the concept of balancing interests, taking interest balance as an important foundation point in intellectual property judicial protection, coordinating the interests of intellectual creators, commercial users, and the public, harmonizing the relationships between incentivizing creation, promoting industrial development, and protecting basic cultural rights and interests, so that all interested parties benefit together and develop in a balanced manner. Strengthen the concept of correctness in initial adjudication, attaching great importance to improving the accuracy rate of first-instance initial adjudications, enabling parties to obtain judicial justice early, increasing the rate of accepting judgments and ceasing appeals, and reducing the appeal rate, thereby promoting social harmony and stability.

3. Leverage advantages and further enhance the leadership role of judicial protection of intellectual property. Continue to deeply implement the national intellectual property strategy concept and goal of giving full play to the leadership role of judicial protection of intellectual property, enhance the firmness and consciousness of implementing this strategic goal, and ensure the scientificity and accuracy of implementation. Adapt to the new situation and new requirements after the formation of the socialist legal system with Chinese characteristics, pay more attention to judicial protection of intellectual property, ensure the implementation of intellectual property laws, and promote socialist rule of law concepts. Pay more attention to the stability and predictability of the application of intellectual property laws, attach importance to procedural guarantees and process transparency, attach importance to the exemplary role of prior typical cases, maximize the provision of stable and foreseeable expectations for stakeholders, and maximize their avoidance of troubles caused by inconsistent judicial standards, actively creating a good legal environment, investment environment, and market environment. Pay more attention to long-term protection mechanisms, attach importance to consistent law enforcement, attach importance to creating a long-term protection mechanism that is persistent, and avoid changing or even damaging the long-term enforcement of the law for the sake of a temporary matter or a single incident. Pay more attention to equal protection, attach importance to the integrated enforcement of intellectual property laws, and resolutely curb local protectionism. Pay more attention to the guiding and orienting function of judgments, attach importance to promoting the socialist core value system in judgments, pay attention to organically combining legal evaluation with moral evaluation, lead mainstream social values, regard the maintenance of public morality as an important value pursuit of judicial protection, and enhance the whole society's intellectual property rule-of-law culture of respecting knowledge, advocating innovation, and acting in good faith and according to law.

II. Strengthen the Adjudication of Cultural Intellectual Property Cases, Promote Cultural Innovation and Cultivate New Cultural Business Forms, and Actively Promote the Great Development and Prosperity of Socialist Culture

4. Attach great importance to the adjudication of cultural intellectual property cases and strengthen the protection of cultural intellectual property according to law. China has formed a cultural legal system with the Copyright Law, the Intangible Cultural Heritage Law, the Regulations on the Protection of Computer Software, the Regulations on the Protection of the Right to Network Dissemination of Information, and other laws and administrative regulations as the backbone. The adjudication of cultural intellectual property cases has become an important aspect of intellectual property adjudication. Earnestly implement the central government's policies and measures on vigorously developing public cultural undertakings and accelerating the development of the cultural industry, formulate and improve relevant judicial interpretations and judicial policies, attach great importance to cultural adjudication work, fully leverage the role of intellectual property adjudication in regulating, guiding, promoting, and guaranteeing cultural construction, stimulate the continuous burst of cultural creativity of the whole nation, enrich the people's social and cultural life, protect the people's basic cultural rights and interests, promote the leapfrog development of the cultural industry, and enhance China's overall cultural strength and international competitiveness. Attach great importance to the protection of new types of intellectual property involved in the cultural industry, and actively promote the cultural industry to become a pillar industry of the national economy. In particular, strengthen copyright protection in industrial fields such as publishing and distribution, film and television production, advertising, performing arts, entertainment, and design according to law, and promote the growth and expansion of traditional cultural industries. Deeply research and vigorously strengthen copyright protection for strategic emerging cultural industries such as cultural creativity, digital publishing, mobile multimedia, animation and games, software, and databases, cultivate new cultural business forms, expand new fields for cultural industry development, cultivate new growth points for the national economy, and enhance China's overall cultural strength and competitiveness. Closely monitor new issues arising from information technology development such as the "triple play" of telecommunications networks, radio and television networks, and the internet, and while protecting copyright interests, pay attention to promoting the development of emerging industries and promoting the improvement of China's informatization level.

5. Strengthen the protection of the rights of cultural creators and ensure the full flow of cultural creation sources. Properly handle the relationship between the originality and the height of originality of works, both maintaining the unity of the basic standards for granting copyright protection to works and paying attention to grasping the characteristics of various works and adapting to the special needs of relevant protection fields, so that the intensity of protection is coordinated with the height of originality. Properly apply the general provisions of the Copyright Law on copyright to promptly protect creators' new rights and interests. Properly handle the relationship between personal works, works made for hire, and legal entity works, both maximizing the protection of authors' rights and encouraging creative enthusiasm, and protecting the legitimate rights and interests of legal entities or other organizations according to law. Properly use the dichotomy of idea and expression, pay attention to the relativity of the distinction between idea and expression, and reasonably define the scope of protection of works. Attach great importance to the protection of the rights of disseminators, fully protect the legitimate rights and interests of publishers, performers, producers of sound recordings and video recordings, radio stations, and television stations, and promote the dissemination and utilization of works. Actively explore legal protection of rights and interests involved in variety shows, sports programs, etc., and reasonably balance the interests of all relevant parties.

6. Strengthen copyright protection in the network environment, and properly handle the relationship between protecting copyright and promoting the development of the information network industry and ensuring information dissemination. Accurately grasp the spirit and essence of laws, administrative regulations, and judicial interpretations regarding copyright protection in the network environment, especially accurately grasp the balance of interests among rights holders, network service providers, and the public. It is necessary to strengthen copyright protection in the network environment, while paying attention to promoting information network technology innovation and business model development, ensuring the public interest. Correctly grasp the distinction between the provision of works, performances, and sound recordings/video recordings and the provision of network services, properly handle relationships such as exemption and liability of network service providers, the "notice and takedown" rule and fault-based liability, and the difference between network service providers' infringement fault and general infringement fault. Where network service provision behavior meets the statutory exemption conditions, the network service provider shall not bear liability for infringement compensation; although it does not fully meet the statutory exemption conditions, if the network service provider does not have fault, it shall also not bear liability for infringement compensation. According to the characteristics and reality of the information network environment, accurately grasp the determination of infringement fault for network service provision behavior. On the one hand, the fault standard for obvious infringement facts should be used to determine fault, not making network service providers bear general prior review obligations and higher duty of care; on the other hand, appropriately mobilize the initiative of network service providers to actively prevent infringement and cooperate with rights holders to prevent infringement. Maintain the basic value of the "notice and takedown" rule. Except for circumstances where it can be determined that the network service provider has knowledge or should have known based on obvious infringement facts, the liability for infringement compensation of network service providers shall be premised on the prior application of the "notice and takedown" rule. It is necessary to prevent lowering the fault determination standard for network service providers, making the "notice and takedown" rule a dead letter; and also prevent network service providers from being passive and slack in responding to infringement by third parties using their network services, abusing the "notice and takedown" rule.

7. Properly handle the relationship between technology neutrality and the determination of infringement, achieving a harmonious unity between effective copyright protection and promoting technological innovation and industrial development. Both accurately grasp the value neutrality and multi-purpose nature of technology as a tool means, and fully understand the behavior and purpose of technology providers reflected and embodied by the technology. Neither unconditionally attribute the infringement consequences brought by technology to technology providers, stifling technological innovation and development; nor absolutize technology neutrality, simply using technology neutrality as a shield to improperly exempt from infringement liability. For technologies with substantial non-infringing commercial uses, strictly grasp the conditions for technology providers to bear joint liability, and cannot presume that technology providers should know the existence of specific direct infringement acts; they only bear joint liability with direct infringers when they have other assisting or inducing acts. For technologies that have no other substantial commercial uses except primarily for copyright infringement, it can be presumed that the technology provider should know the existence of specific direct infringement acts, and they shall bear joint liability with the direct infringers. When hearing copyright cases involving emerging industries such as network copyright and "triple play," it is particularly important to accurately grasp the spirit of technology neutrality, which is conducive to promoting technological and commercial innovation while preventing the commission of infringement in the name of technology neutrality.

8. Properly apply the limitations and exceptions to copyright, correctly determine the legality of the alleged infringing acts, promote commercial and technological innovation, and fully guarantee the people's basic cultural rights and interests. Correctly determine fair use and statutory license acts, and protect the legitimate use and dissemination of works according to law. In special circumstances where it is truly necessary to promote technological innovation and commercial development, consider factors such as the nature and purpose of the use of the work, the nature of the used work, the quantity and quality of the used portion, and the impact of the use on the potential market or value of the work. If the use does not conflict with the normal use of the work and does not unreasonably prejudice the legitimate interests of the author, it may be deemed as fair use. For artistic works set up or displayed in outdoor public places, copying, painting, photographing, or recording, and subsequently using the results in a reasonable manner and within a reasonable scope, regardless of whether the use has a commercial purpose, may be deemed as fair use.

9. Comprehensively apply various legal means to actively promote the protection, inheritance, development, and utilization of intangible cultural heritage, and promote the transformation of China's rich cultural resources into strong cultural competitiveness. Intangible cultural heritage is an important foundation and bond for consolidating national spirit, inheriting national culture, maintaining cultural diversity, and promoting social harmony and sustainable development, and is an important source of cultural innovation. Adhering to the principle of emphasizing both inheritance and innovation, protection and utilization, actively protect intangible cultural heritage such as folk literature and art, traditional knowledge, and genetic resources, based on existing laws and legislative spirit, and fairly and reasonably coordinate and balance the interests of all parties in the process of discovery, collation, inheritance, protection, development, and utilization. Adhere to the principle of respect; when utilizing intangible cultural heritage, its form and connotation should be respected, and intangible cultural heritage shall not be used in ways such as distortion or denigration. Adhere to the principle of source disclosure; when utilizing intangible cultural heritage, the source of information should be indicated in an appropriate manner. Encourage informed consent and benefit sharing; users of intangible cultural heritage should, as far as possible, obtain informed consent from the keepers, providers, holders, or relevant protection departments, and share the benefits of use with them in an appropriate manner. Comprehensively apply various means such as copyright law, trademark law, patent law, and anti-unfair competition law to actively protect the inheritance and commercial development and utilization of intangible cultural heritage.

10. Make full use of copyright protection means to protect works of folk literature and art according to law. The copyright protection of works of folk literature and art should be conducive to the inheritance of folk literature and art, giving play to their role in consolidating national spirit and maintaining the spiritual home of the nation, and also conducive to innovation and utilization, enhancing the influence of Chinese culture. Works of folk literature and art may be jointly enjoyed by the specific ethnic group or regional group that created and inherited the work; the relevant government departments of the specific ethnic group or region have the right to exercise protection rights on their behalf. For the preservers and collators of works of folk literature and art, their right to be named in an appropriate manner should be respected. Using elements or materials of folk literature and art for subsequent creation does not require permission or payment of fees; if a work with originality is formed, the author may obtain complete copyright protection according to law, but the source of the materials of the work should be indicated. Improper use of works of folk literature and art that damages the spiritual rights and interests of specific ethnic groups or regional groups may result in a people's court ordering the improper user to bear corresponding civil liability.

11. Effectively use legal means such as trademark law and patent law to protect the commercial value of intangible cultural heritage and promote the transformation of natural and human resources with local characteristics into real productivity. If applying for trademark registration of the names, logos, etc. of intangible cultural heritage constitutes improper use such as distortion, denigration, or misleading of intangible cultural heritage, and damages the spiritual rights and interests of specific ethnic groups or regional groups, it may be deemed as having other adverse effects and prohibited from being used as a trademark; if it has already been used and caused adverse effects, the people's court may, according to the specific circumstances of the case, order the user to bear civil liability such as ceasing use, making an apology, and eliminating the impact. If the names, logos, etc. of intangible cultural heritage constitute geographical indications, they may be protected as prior rights depending on the specific circumstances. If traditional knowledge and genetic resources in intangible cultural heritage constitute trade secrets, others are prohibited from stealing, illegally disclosing, or using them. If genetic resources are obtained or utilized in violation of laws and regulations, and an invention-creation is completed relying on such genetic resources and a patent is granted, the patentee's accusation of patent infringement against others may not be supported.

III. Strengthen the Protection of Scientific and Technological Achievements Rights, Promote Scientific and Technological Progress and Innovation, and Enhance Independent Innovation Capability

12. Strengthen the protection of scientific and technological intellectual property such as patents, new plant varieties, and integrated circuit layout designs according to law, and actively promote scientific and technological progress and innovation. Based on the new trends in scientific and technological progress and new needs in economic development, with the important goals of improving China's original innovation capability and enhancing integrated innovation and the ability to introduce, digest, absorb, and re-innovate, accurately implement the legislative spirit of the Patent Law and correctly conduct infringement determination, strengthen the protection of intellectual property in key core technologies, basic frontier fields, and strategic emerging industries, promote technological breakthroughs and innovation, advance the optimization and upgrading of traditional industries, accelerate the cultivation and development of strategic emerging industries, accelerate the formation of leading and pillar industries, and enhance the core competitiveness of enterprises and the country. Increase the protection of scientific and technological intellectual property in the cultural field, give play to the engine role of scientific and technological innovation in cultural development, promote the improvement of the technological equipment level of the cultural industry, enhance the core competitiveness of the cultural industry, and promote Chinese culture to go global.

13. Properly implement the judicial policy of appropriately balancing strict and lenient patent protection, and vigorously enhance the capability for independent innovation. When determining the specific scope and intensity of patent protection, due consideration should be given to the characteristics and innovation realities of patents in different technical fields, so as to meet the innovation needs, characteristics, and development realities of different technical fields. Adhere to the principle of compromise interpretation for the scope of protection of invention and utility model patents, and precisely define the scope of patent protection. Pay attention to the limiting effect of the patent's inventive purpose on the scope of protection; technical solutions that possess the defects or deficiencies of the prior art that the patent seeks to overcome should not be included within the scope of protection. For pioneering inventions characterized by a high degree of innovation, substantial research and development investment, and a breakthrough and driving effect on economic growth, relatively higher protection intensity and a broader scope of equivalent protection should be granted. For improvement inventions with a relatively lower degree of innovation, the scope of equivalent protection should be appropriately limited.

14. Correctly apply the methods for determining patent infringement, and increase the intensity of curbing patent infringement. Accurately grasp the determination rules for all technical features comparison, prosecution history estoppel, and dedication for invention and utility model patent infringement determination, and continue to explore and improve the conditions for applying the doctrine of equivalents. The doctrine of equivalents should take as necessary conditions that the means, functions, and effects are substantially identical and that it is obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art, so as to prevent simple and mechanical application of the doctrine of equivalents or improper expansion of its scope of application. The prior art defense rule is applicable in both equivalent infringement and literal infringement. Accurately grasp the determination method for design patent infringement, which involves observing the overall design features and making a comprehensive judgment on the overall visual effect, taking the general consumer of the design product as the subject of judgment, taking the distinctive design features of the design as the core, and taking the identity or similarity of the overall visual effect of the product's exterior design as the fundamental standard for determining the establishment of infringement. Correctly apply the prior art and prior design defenses. Where the alleged infringer claims a prior art or prior design defense based on an obvious combination of one prior art technical solution or one prior design recorded in a prior art document with common general knowledge or conventional design, such claim shall be supported. Where the alleged infringer claims that its implementation of a technical solution or design in a conflicting application does not constitute patent infringement, this may be judged by reference to the examination and determination standards for the prior art or prior design defense.

15. Properly hear cases involving infringement of invention patents for product manufacturing methods, and legally protect method invention patent rights. While appropriately considering the practical difficulties of method patent holders in enforcing their rights, also take into account the legitimate rights and interests of the alleged infringer in protecting its trade secrets. Legally apply the rule of reversed burden of proof for new product manufacturing method patents. Where the product obtained by using the patented method and the technical solution for manufacturing the product were not known to the public before the patent application date, the alleged infringer who manufactures an identical product shall bear the burden of proving that its product manufacturing method is different from the patented method. Where the product obtained by using the patented method is not a new product, and the patentee can prove that the alleged infringer has manufactured an identical product, but despite reasonable efforts, still cannot prove that the alleged infringer actually used the patented method, however, based on the specific circumstances of the case, combined with known facts and common life experience, it can be determined that the identical product was very likely made by the patented method, then in accordance with the relevant provisions of the judicial interpretation on civil evidence, the patentee shall no longer be required to provide further evidence, and the alleged infringer shall be required to provide evidence that its manufacturing method is different from the patented method. In view of the actual difficulty of proving method patent infringement, legally adopt evidence preservation measures to appropriately alleviate the burden of proof on the method patent holder. Pay attention to protecting the interests of the respondent, and prevent parties from abusing the evidence preservation system to illegally obtain others' trade secrets. Where the alleged infringer provides evidence that its manufacturing method is different from the patented method and involves trade secrets, measures should be taken to protect them during examination and judgment.

16. Properly handle the relationship between protecting patent rights and preventing abuse of rights, and legally regulate the abuse of patent rights and the abuse of the pre-litigation injunction system. While legally protecting patent rights and safeguarding the parties' right of action, pay attention to preventing patentees from exercising their rights in obvious contradiction to the legal purpose, improperly harming competitors, hindering fair competition, and disrupting market order. Where a patentee knowingly has a patent that belongs to prior art or prior design, but still maliciously sends infringement warnings to bona fide implementers and their transaction counterparts or abuses its right of action, and this constitutes infringement, the victim's claim for damages may be supported depending on the circumstances. Strictly control the legal conditions and strengthen procedural safeguards; carefully and legally take pre-litigation measures to cease patent infringement. Adhere to the premise that the facts are relatively clear and infringement is easy to determine before taking pre-litigation cessation measures. For acts where a more complex technical comparison is required to determine the likelihood of infringement, it is generally inadvisable to order pre-litigation cessation measures. Where conditions permit, accurately determine the likelihood of infringement by hearing the opinions of both the applicant and the respondent as much as possible. Where a decision on a request for invalidation declaring the patent in question invalid has already been made, pre-litigation measures to cease patent infringement shall generally not be ordered.

17. Strengthen the protection of new plant variety rights, promote agricultural science and technology innovation, and accelerate the transformation of agricultural development methods. Increase protection for major agricultural scientific and technological achievements and new plant varieties with independent intellectual property rights, promote the enhancement of independent innovation capabilities, advance agricultural science and technology progress, and improve comprehensive agricultural production capacity, risk resistance, and market competitiveness. Strictly protect the interests of variety rights holders according to law, vigorously promote the breeding of varieties and the transformation of innovation achievements, and develop modern agriculture. Intensify the crackdown on infringement of new plant variety rights. For acts of producing, selling, or repeatedly using reproductive material of an authorized variety for commercial purposes, promptly stop them according to law; for acts of counterfeiting others' authorized varieties, also handle them as disputes over infringement of new plant variety rights. Legally examine the variety rights holder's application for evidence preservation, actively adopt evidence preservation measures, and ensure that the variety rights holder obtains judicial relief in a timely manner. When adopting evidence preservation measures for the alleged infringing reproductive material, follow the corresponding technical procedures as much as possible to ensure the objectivity and representativeness of the sampling; however, the validity of the evidence preservation shall not be simply denied on the grounds that relevant professional and technical personnel were not invited to assist in the sampling. Pay attention to legally protecting the legitimate rights and interests of farmers, and maintaining agricultural and rural stability. Correctly distinguish between large-scale seed producers who are variety producers and managers and ordinary individuals and rural contract operators who engage in farming. While legally exempting ordinary individuals and rural contract operators who engage in farming from liability for infringement for self-propagation and self-use of reproductive material of an authorized variety, prevent large-scale seed producers who are essentially variety producers and managers from evading legal sanctions.

IV. Strengthening Trademark Protection, Cultivating and Maintaining Well-known Brands, and Actively Promoting Competitive, Innovative, and Inclusive Growth of the Socialist Market Economy

18. Legally strengthen trademark protection. Trademark protection must be conducive to encouraging fair competition, clarifying the boundaries between commercial identifiers, curbing malicious preemptive registration of others' well-known commercial identifiers and "free-riding on well-known brands" behavior, and providing a harmonious and relaxed legal environment for the creation and development of well-known brands, thereby assisting in cultivating well-known brands and enhancing the comprehensive competitiveness of enterprises, and promoting China's rapid transformation from a manufacturing powerhouse to a brand powerhouse. Based on the degree of fame and distinctiveness of the trademark, appropriately apply discretionary legal standards such as trademark similarity, goods similarity, prior use and having certain influence trademarks, and obtaining trademark registration by fraud or other improper means, properly grasp whether the trademark applicant or registrant has a genuine intention to use the mark, and determine subjective bad faith in conjunction with "free-riding on well-known brands" behavior during trademark use, fully utilize the relevant provisions of the Trademark Law, increase the intensity of curbing improper acts such as malicious preemptive registration and "free-riding on well-known brands", and fully reflect the legal orientation of trademark protection.

19. Properly handle the relationship between trademark similarity and similarity of constituent elements of trademarks, and accurately grasp the legal standard for determining trademark similarity. Whether trademarks are considered similar depends on the specific circumstances of the case. Generally, if the constituent elements of the relevant trademarks as a whole are similar, the trademarks may be deemed similar. If the constituent elements of the relevant trademarks as a whole are not similar, but the trademark whose rights are claimed has a much higher degree of fame than the alleged infringing trademark, the main parts may be compared to determine similarity. Properly handle the relationship between maximizing the demarcation of boundaries between commercial identifiers and allowing the appropriate coexistence of trademarks with similar constituent elements under special circumstances. Where the relevant trademarks both have a relatively high degree of fame, or the coexistence of the relevant trademarks was formed under special conditions, the determination of trademark similarity should also be comprehensively judged based on the actual usage status, usage history, the perception status of the relevant public, and the subjective state of the users, paying attention to respecting the market pattern that has objectively formed, and preventing the simple equation of similarity of trademark constituent elements with trademark similarity, so as to achieve inclusive development among operators.

20. Fully consider the correlation of the goods on which the trademarks are used, and accurately grasp the standard for determining goods similarity. When determining goods similarity, reference may be made to the Classification of Similar Goods, but greater respect should be given to market reality. Use the general awareness of the relevant public as the standard, combined with the functions, uses, production departments, sales channels, consumer objects, and other factors of the goods, to correctly determine goods similarity within the meaning of the Trademark Law. Where the trademark whose rights are claimed has been actually used and has a certain degree of fame, full consideration should be given to the correlation between the goods when determining goods similarity. Goods that the relevant public believes have a specific correlation based on their usual perception and general transaction perception of the goods may, depending on the circumstances, be included within the scope of similar goods.

21. Standardize the determination and protection of well-known trademarks, and effectively strengthen the protection of well-known trademarks. The purpose of protecting well-known trademarks is to appropriately expand the scope and intensity of protection for trademarks with a relatively high degree of fame, not to rate or grant honorary titles. Where a party claims protection for a well-known trademark and meets the conditions for protection and it is indeed necessary, it should be determined and protected according to law. For well-known trademarks that are widely known to the general public, the trademark owner's burden of proof for the well-known status of the trademark should be alleviated based on the well-known facts. Determining a trademark as well-known does not require a uniform degree of fame, but the scope and intensity of protection for a well-known trademark should correspond to its distinctiveness and degree of fame. The stronger the distinctiveness and the higher the degree of fame of a well-known trademark, the broader the cross-class protection scope and the stronger the protection intensity should be given. Carefully implement the provisions of judicial interpretations, accurately grasp the scope of protection for well-known trademarks, strengthen strict control over the factual determination of well-known trademarks, adhere to the pre-judgment review system, prevent parties from engaging in fraud, and prevent false litigation for the purpose of fraudulently obtaining a well-known trademark determination.

22. Properly determine defenses against trademark infringement, and safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of bona fide operators. Trademark infringement requires the use of an identical or similar trademark in the sense of a commercial identifier. Where the alleged infringer uses an identical or similar mark in good faith and reasonably for the purpose of describing or indicating the characteristics of its products or services, it may be determined as fair use according to law. Where the registered trademark of the trademark owner consists of a reproduction, imitation, or translation of another person's unregistered well-known trademark in China, a preemptive registration of a trademark of the principal or representative, or a preemptive registration by improper means of a trademark that another person has used and has a certain influence, and the prior user of the trademark who is allegedly infringing raises a defense on this ground, such defense shall be supported.

23. Properly handle the relationship between substance and procedure, and strengthen the substantive resolution of trademark authorization and confirmation disputes. Procedure has its independent legal value, but it must also be oriented towards and have as its ultimate goal the resolution of substantive issues and the realization of substantive justice. Substantive justice is both the goal and direction of procedural operation, and requires procedural justice as its support and guarantee. While attaching great importance to procedural justice and preventing the one-sided pursuit of substantive justice while neglecting procedural justice, it is also necessary to take substantive justice as the ultimate goal and prevent mechanical justice. Where a party's exercise of procedural rights is flawed and may affect its significant substantive rights and interests, or even potentially lead to the loss of relief opportunities without other remedies, opportunities for remedy may be granted depending on the specific circumstances of the case. Pay attention to the substantive resolution of trademark authorization and confirmation disputes, avoid unnecessary procedural repetition, shelving substantive issues, and avoiding contradictions. Where substantive judgments can be made on whether a trademark should be registered or whether it should be revoked, a clear judgment may be made in the reasoning of the judgment, providing clear guidance for the sued administrative agency to make a new decision.

V. Legally Regulating the Order of Competition, Cultivating a Culture of Free, Fair, Honest, and Law-abiding Competition, and Creating a Fair, Orderly, and Vibrant Market Environment

24. Strengthen the trial of unfair competition cases, and safeguard market fair competition. Properly handle the relationship between specialized intellectual property laws and the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. While stimulating innovation, also encourage fair competition. The supplementary protection role of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law shall not conflict with the legislative policies of specialized intellectual property laws. In areas where specialized intellectual property laws have provided exhaustive provisions, the Anti-Unfair Competition Law in principle shall not provide additional protection, allowing free use and free competition. However, within the scope compatible with the legislative policies of specialized intellectual property laws, protection may still be provided from the perspective of curbing unfair competition. Properly handle the relationship between the general provisions and specific provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. While fully utilizing the flexibility and adaptability of the general provisions to effectively curb various novel and ever-emerging unfair competition acts, prevent the arbitrary application of the general provisions to avoid hindering free and fair competition in the market. Strictly control the conditions for applying the general provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. In areas where the specific provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law have expressly prohibited certain acts, only the specific provisions shall be used to regulate similar unfair competition acts; in principle, the general provisions should not be applied to expand the scope of application. For acts not expressly prohibited by the specific provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, if they cause harm to the legitimate rights and interests of other business operators and are indeed contrary to the principle of good faith and generally accepted business ethics, thus possessing unfairness, and if failing to stop them is insufficient to maintain fair competition order, the general provisions may be applied to regulate them. Correctly grasp the criteria for evaluating the principle of good faith and generally accepted business ethics, using the standard of economic person ethics generally recognized and accepted in specific commercial fields as the yardstick, avoiding the simple equation of the principle of good faith and generally accepted business ethics with personal morality or social ethics.

25. Legally strengthen the protection of trade secrets, effectively stop acts of infringing trade secrets, and create a safe and trustworthy legal environment for enterprise innovation and investment. Based on the specific circumstances of the case, reasonably grasp the standard of proof for secrecy and improper means, and appropriately alleviate the difficulties of trade secret holders in enforcing their rights. Where the right holder provides preponderant evidence of secrecy or makes a sufficiently reasonable explanation or clarification of the differences between the trade secret information it claims and the information in the public domain, secrecy may be established. Where the trade secret right holder provides evidence that the information of the alleged party is identical or substantially identical to its trade secret and that the alleged party has the conditions to access or illegally obtain the trade secret, based on the specific circumstances of the case or known facts and common life experience, it can be determined that there is a relatively high probability that the alleged party adopted improper means, the fact that the alleged party obtained the trade secret by improper means may be presumed to be established, unless the alleged party proves that it obtained the information through lawful means. Accurately define the scope of protection of the trade secret based on trade secret information that meets the statutory conditions, with each individual unit of trade secret information constituting an independent object of protection. Improve the trial and cross-examination methods in trade secret cases. For evidence involving trade secrets, measures such as displaying only to agents, phased display, and requiring confidentiality undertakings should be attempted to limit the scope of knowledge and dissemination channels of the trade secret, and prevent secondary disclosure during the trial. Properly handle the relationship between civil infringement proceedings and criminal proceedings for trade secrets. While paying attention to the correlation between the two types of proceedings, also pay attention to their mutual independence. While protecting trade secrets according to law, also prevent operators from maliciously initiating criminal proceedings to interfere with and suppress competitors.

26. Properly handle the relationship between protecting trade secrets and freedom of employment, non-compete obligations of secret-holders, and reasonable flow of talent, safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of workers in employment and entrepreneurship, and legally promote the reasonable flow of labor. The knowledge, experience, and skills that employees acquire and accumulate during their work, except where they constitute the employer's trade secrets, form part of their personality, and employees have the freedom to use them independently after leaving their posts. Where an employee does not violate non-compete obligations and does not infringe trade secrets, and uses the knowledge, experience, and skills learned at the original employer to serve another entity that has a competitive relationship with the original employer, it is generally not appropriate to simply determine that it constitutes unfair competition based on the general provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Properly handle the relationship between trade secret protection and non-compete agreements. A non-compete agreement is premised on the existence of protectable trade secrets, but the two have different legal bases and behavioral manifestations. Violation of non-compete obligations does not equate to infringement of trade secrets, and the duration of non-compete does not equal the duration of confidentiality. Where a plaintiff files an infringement lawsuit on the grounds of infringement of trade secrets, this is not restricted by the existence of a pre-existing non-compete agreement.

27. Strengthen the trial of monopoly cases, promptly and effectively stop monopolistic conduct, enhance market vitality, promote the improvement of market structure, and the healthy development of the market economy. Strengthen the effects-based approach of the Anti-Monopoly Law, comprehensively consider various relevant factors, comprehensively evaluate the anti-competitive and pro-competitive effects of the alleged monopolistic conduct, and determine monopolistic conduct according to law. Pay attention to leveraging the role of economics experts and professional institutions, and explore ways and means of introducing economic analysis methods. Reasonably allocate the burden of proof among parties in civil monopoly dispute cases according to the different types of monopolistic conduct. For monopoly agreements that clearly have the effect of seriously excluding or restricting competition, the victim may no longer be required to prove that the agreement has the effect of excluding or restricting competition. For public utility enterprises and other operators with exclusive operational qualifications that abuse market dominance, the burden of proof on the victim may be appropriately alleviated depending on the specific circumstances of the case.

VI. Strengthening the Construction of the Intellectual Property Litigation System, and Improving the Trial System and Working Mechanism

28. Deeply understand the characteristics and patterns of intellectual property cases, and establish and perfect a dispute resolution mechanism suitable for the characteristics of intellectual property cases. Correctly grasp the working principle of "mediation first, combining mediation and adjudication." Given the highly professional and technical nature of intellectual property cases, actively guide parties to choose dispute resolution methods such as entrusted mediation, expert mediation, and industry mediation. Adhere to the principle of voluntary mediation according to law, and do not force mediation or delay to promote mediation against the will of the parties. For cases where the parties or the relevant industry have high expectations for distinguishing right from wrong, or have strong demands for clarifying rules, or have a high degree of acceptance of judgments, choose to resolve the dispute by judgment as much as possible, fully leveraging the guiding and orienting function of judicial decisions. Leverage the role of science and technology experts in resolving disputes, and improve the mechanism for solving technical problems in intellectual property cases.

29. Continue to improve the intellectual property trial system and mechanism, and fully leverage the comprehensive effectiveness of judicial protection of intellectual property rights. In accordance with the requirements of the National Intellectual Property Strategy, actively promote the pilot work of centralized trial of intellectual property civil, administrative, and criminal cases by intellectual property trial divisions, establish a coordination mechanism for intellectual property civil, administrative, and criminal trials, improve judicial efficiency, unify judicial standards, and give full play to the overall protection effectiveness, striving to build an intellectual property trial system with optimized resources, scientific operation, and high efficiency and authority. Efforts shall be strengthened to coordinate and cooperate with public security organs, procuratorial organs, and intellectual property administrative law enforcement organs to form a joint force for protection. Optimize the layout of jurisdiction over intellectual property cases, appropriately increase the number of basic-level courts with jurisdiction over general intellectual property cases, encourage intermediate and basic-level courts to conduct cross-regional centralized jurisdiction by designated areas according to work needs, and rationally allocate trial resources.

30. Uphold the unity of the rule of law and promote a unified and open market. Improve the case jurisdiction system, strengthen supervision and restraint, and appropriately adopt measures such as elevating jurisdiction and designating jurisdiction from other localities to effectively curb local protectionism and departmental protectionism, ensuring fair trial of cases. Where a decision is made to elevate jurisdiction or designate jurisdiction from another locality, the original court with jurisdiction shall correctly treat such decision and promptly transfer the case. Effectively strengthen trial supervision, give play to the error-correcting function of second instance and retrial proceedings, and avoid accommodating erroneous judgments for the sake of trial performance evaluation indicators. With respect to cases designated for retrial, the relevant retrial court shall correctly understand and earnestly treat the retrial instruction, and correct errors in accordance with the law. Where a court disregards the retrial instruction, delays the retrial, or fails to execute the retrial instruction without justifiable reasons, strict disciplinary action shall be taken, and where circumstances are serious, a notice of criticism shall be issued. Further improve the working mechanism, appropriately increase coordination and guidance on related intellectual property cases, and maintain the uniformity of adjudication standards.
